title: Anyone else using AI with Unreal 5.8?
author: Will_X_Intent
selftext: I'd love to have a discussion on what you've found that works great, what works well, what kinda works, and stuff AI just completely fails at.

comments.author: crumbaker
comments.body: Curious how it is at its current state, I've made a commercial game with it, but only with ai art.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body:
Fable can figure out how to do a lot of things without super detailed prompting, but will eat a lot of tokens thinking.  Opus created a contextual tooltip system for me 90% correct in one prompt.  Fable has been having Sonnet build rough levels for me using modular dungeon assets.  It's... iffy, and spends a lot of time failing.  

I've noticed all the models will waste a lot of time and tokens chasing bugs they dont understand well if you don't intervene.  If they make a mistake, it's better if you coach them through it.

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body:
Yep. It’s great. 

 The 5.8 MCP with Claude code can basically drive the engine for you.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: If Fable wasn't so expensive and token hungry, my life would be much easier.

replies.author: MidSerpent
replies.body: I use Opus most of the time and only use Fable for deep thinking

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: When you get used to how few mistakes Fable makes and how quickly it fixes those mistakes, Opus is hard to go back to.

replies.author: DrStrangeLaughTV
replies.body: I will try it out for a few days, but I have already been very impressed with opus with basic rules and skills that I added.

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body:
I spent a couple weeks designing the core skill system with Opus, then another week or so copy pasting C++ into the project before 5.8 forced me to use Cowork.  Now I'll never go back to chat (chat's very context inefficient) and I can hand off huge tasks to Cowork or Code.  Wish I could have just Fable work the entire time.  

I kinda feel like my design documents are robust enough that I could just run Fable for a week non-stop and the game would be pretty close to what I want.  Close enough that I would have have to focus on polish.

My next goal is to figure out how to use AI with metahuman and generating animations.

comments.author: Char_Zulu
comments.body: Yea give it unreal’s source code. 1000x more efficient. And it can make addons

comments.author: thewowcollector
comments.body: Claude says it has no access to the Unreal Engine. How do you get around that.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: update to 5.8 then install the plugin and then figure out how to make it work in cowork or code.  I wrote a guide to cowork on this sub I believe.

replies.body: I wonder too.  The MCP doesn't come with skills ( i think) so my AI at least is often stumbling around trying to figure stuff out.  It looks like NWIRO might reduce those headaches.

comments.author: hellomistershifty
comments.body: I don’t do asset generation but ue-mcp is free and solid for controlling the editor and letting your agent “talk to” assets. Just edit it to turn off some annoying messages it adds

comments.author: Ok_Bill7731
comments.body: for engine stuff the 5.8 mcp with claude code is genuinely good. it wires up systems faster than i can type. where it falls apart for me is the world/sim side, the npc behavior and how a place reacts to what the player actually does. i prototype that part in worldos before committing any of it to the engine, you poke the world and watch it respond, way faster than stubbing it all out in c++. its hosted so no offline, and it wont hold up for anything mechanically deep, more of a sketch tool. still saves me building three systems i end up deleting.
